headline: CAMECO Q2 REVENUE BEATS AT C$814M BUT EPS MISSES — Shares Gain as $85/lb Uranium Offsets Lower Delivery Volumes
snippet: Cameco Corporation (TSX/NYSE: CCJ) reported Q2 2026 results on July 31 that beat revenue expectations handily — C$814 million versus the analyst consensus of C$592 million — but missed on adjusted EPS at C$0.18 versus the C$0.28 estimate, with shares trading up as investors focused on the revenue beat over the earnings shortfall. The delivery miss (7.1 million lbs in Q2 versus 8.7 million in the prior year) reflects Cameco's disciplined contracting strategy rather than operational problems: the company continues to deliver under long-term contracts at realized prices averaging approximately $85.18 per pound, a 17% year-on-year improvement. The earnings miss was driven by a significant decline in equity earnings from the Westinghouse investment, which had a one-time construction project contribution in the year-ago quarter. For uranium investors, the message is clear: Cameco's core uranium segment is performing well at $85+ spot prices, its disciplined delivery cadence is intact, and Westinghouse's drag is a non-recurring comparison issue. Full-year guidance remains unchanged.

headline: SILVER +1.51% TO $59.08 AS GOLD SLIPS — 46M oz Annual Deficit Widens; Gold-Silver Ratio Signals Rotation Trade
snippet: Silver outperformed gold on July 31, 2026, rising 1.51% to $59.08 per ounce as gold slipped 0.42% to $4,086 — a divergence traders are watching as a potential rotation signal. The structural backdrop is supportive: the World Silver Survey 2026 projects a 46.3 million ounce supply deficit, the sixth consecutive annual shortfall and wider than 2025's 40.3 million ounce gap, driven by solar PV, EV, semiconductor, and AI data-centre demand that mine supply cannot match. China's January 2026 reclassification of silver as a strategic material (requiring government export licences) has also tightened the Western supply picture. The gold-silver ratio at approximately 69:1 sits near the top of its 50-year historical range of 60:1–70:1 — a level that has historically preceded periods of silver outperformance. For junior silver developers tracking project economics, $59 silver fundamentally changes the NPV calculus on deposits that were borderline at $25. Primary silver miners and silver-heavy exploration companies on the TSX-V and ASX are the direct beneficiaries of any sustained ratio compression.

headline: AGNICO POSTS RECORD $1.335B FREE CASH FLOW IN Q2 — $3.19 EPS, 856K oz at $4,483 Realized; $625M Returned to Shareholders
snippet: Agnico Eagle Mines (TSX/NYSE: AEM) reported Q2 2026 results on July 29 showing record quarterly free cash flow of $1.335 billion and record shareholder returns of $625 million — $400 million in buybacks plus dividends — as the senior gold producer generated net income of $1.6 billion ($3.19 per share) on gold sales of 835,505 ounces at a realized price of $4,483 per ounce. Adjusted EPS of $3.05 beat the consensus of $2.89, while revenues of $3.8 billion missed estimates by 1.56% but reflected the company's conservative hedging posture. Production of 856,000 ounces for the quarter exceeded internal budget for the second consecutive quarter, though management guided toward the lower end of full-year guidance of 3.3–3.5 million ounces due to a preliminary redesign of the Barnat open pit at Canadian Malartic. The record free cash flow number — $2.66 per share — is the clearest demonstration yet that senior gold producers are generating cash flows that imply single-digit P/FCF multiples at $4,000+ gold, creating the conditions for continued aggressive capital returns and potential M&A.

headline: KINROSS Q2: $727M FREE CASH FLOW, RECORD $2.7B CASH — $0.71 EPS Beats; 2.0M GEO Annual Guidance Reaffirmed (TSX/NYSE: KGC)
snippet: Kinross Gold Corporation (TSX/NYSE: KGC) reported Q2 2026 results on July 29 with net income of $844.2 million ($0.71 per share, beating the $0.66 consensus), revenue of $2.24 billion, and free cash flow of $727 million in the quarter — the second-best quarterly FCF in company history. Kinross ended H1 2026 with over $1.5 billion in cumulative free cash flow and a record cash balance of $2.7 billion with net cash of $1.9 billion, giving the company exceptional financial flexibility at a time when acquisition targets are being evaluated. The company reaffirmed full-year 2026 production guidance of approximately 2.0 million gold equivalent ounces (±5%) and is targeting a return of 40% of free cash flow to shareholders through dividends and buybacks. Kinross shares rose 2.46% in premarket trading following the release. For investors tracking the valuation gap between gold prices and equity multiples, Kinross at $2.7 billion in cash and generating $1.5 billion in H1 FCF represents one of the clearest examples of the capital return cycle accelerating across the senior gold sector.

headline: DPM METALS Q2: RECORD $227M FREE CASH FLOW — Vareš Ramp Drives 94% Revenue Surge; $761M on Balance Sheet (TSX: DPM)
snippet: DPM Metals (TSX: DPM) reported Q2 2026 results on July 30 showing record quarterly free cash flow of $227 million and record net earnings of $230 million ($1.04 per share), as revenue surged 94% year-on-year driven by the addition of the Vareš copper-zinc-gold mine in Bosnia to the producing portfolio. The company generated $271 million in operating cash and ended the quarter with $761.2 million in cash plus an undrawn $400 million revolving credit facility — a fortress balance sheet that positions DPM for further growth capital or M&A. The Vareš polymetallic mine remains on track to achieve full production by year-end 2026. Meanwhile, the June 2026 announcement of the Brevene South Porphyry discovery at Chelopech, Bulgaria — 713 metres at 2.52 g/t AuEq in a fourth district-scale porphyry — adds a high-impact exploration catalyst that the market is only beginning to price in. DPM's combination of record financial performance, fortress balance sheet, and a major new porphyry discovery makes it one of the more compelling mid-tier mining stories in 2026.

headline: LIT ETF JUMPS 4.60% AS ALBEMARLE RALLIES 3.41% — MinRes Bald Hill Delivers First Spodumene After 18-Month Shutdown
snippet: The Global X Lithium & Battery Tech ETF (LIT) surged 4.60% to US$69.81 on July 31, 2026, as Albemarle (NYSE: ALB) gained 3.41% to US$117.76 and SQM (NYSE: SQM) added 1.30% to US$68.43 — a sharp reversal from the sector's July weakness. The equity bounce coincides with a significant operational milestone: Mineral Resources (ASX: MIN) confirmed first spodumene concentrate production at the Bald Hill lithium mine in Western Australia's Goldfields region during July, completing a phased restart from an 18-month care-and-maintenance period. Bald Hill's nameplate capacity of approximately 165,000 dry metric tonnes per annum of 5.1% spodumene concentrate represents a meaningful addition to global SC5/SC6 supply. The restart cost approximately A$20 million and is expected to create around 370 jobs. While lithium spot prices in China remain subdued near CNY 145,000 per tonne — and the LIT bounce looks partly technical rather than driven by fundamental price recovery — the equity sector is beginning to price in a second-half improvement scenario, with Albemarle's Q2 results due August 5.

headline: COPPER SURGES TO $6.44/LB — Codelco Admits "NO POSSIBILITY" of 1.7M-Tonne Target; LME Stocks Fall, China Premium at 4-Year High
snippet: Copper rose to $6.44 per pound in late July 2026 — up 2.49% in a single session — as a combination of structural supply tightening and macro tailwinds converged. Codelco chairman Bernardo Fontaine has explicitly stated there is "no possibility" of the state miner meeting its former 1.7 million tonne per annum production target within five years, with official 2026 guidance at 1.331–1.357 million tonnes — a roughly 25% shortfall from the aspirational level. ICSG data confirms a real and persistent copper supply deficit in 2026, with LME copper inventories falling more than 10,000 tonnes to 262,300 tonnes and nearby LME contracts trading at a $24-per-tonne premium over three-month contracts, signalling near-term scarcity. China's import premiums for copper cathode hit their highest level since 2022. Copper has gained more than 14% year-to-date in 2026 and briefly touched above $6.60 per pound in early June before pulling back. For TSX-V and ASX copper explorers and developers whose projects were modelled at $4.00–$4.50 copper, the current price environment is transformational for project economics.

headline: WESTHAVEN SOUTH ZONE: 27.51m GRADING 14.47 g/t AU + 52 g/t AG — Dundee-Backed BC Infill Confirms High-Grade Continuity (TSXV: WHN)
snippet: Westhaven Gold Corp. (TSXV: WHN) released the fourth batch of assay results from the ongoing 35,000-metre South Zone resource infill drilling program at its Shovelnose gold and silver property in southern British Columbia on July 28, 2026, highlighted by drill hole SNR26-99 returning 27.51 metres grading 14.47 g/t gold and 52 g/t silver. The result demonstrates the consistent grade-thickness characteristics the program has been confirming throughout, with four drill rigs active at the South Zone. Dundee Corporation has committed a minimum of C$30 million to the project, including the fully funded 50,000-metre drill program expected to run through the remainder of 2026. The South Zone infill data is feeding directly into a resource estimate update and pre-feasibility study, with continued high-grade confirmations at widths like 27.51 metres significantly improving confidence in the deposit geometry. At $4,000+ gold and $59 silver, the combined grade in gold-equivalent terms makes Shovelnose one of the highest-grade undeveloped deposits in British Columbia — a jurisdiction with established permitting pathways and proximity to infrastructure.

headline: FLORIDA CANYON: US$0.8B AFTER-TAX FREE CASH FLOW, RESERVES +74% TO 1.1M oz — Integra Feasibility Extends Nevada Gold Mine Life (TSXV: ITR)
snippet: Integra Resources Corp. (TSXV: ITR) filed a feasibility study and updated life-of-mine plan for its operating Florida Canyon Mine in Pershing County, Nevada on July 30, 2026, with the technical report delivering a material upgrade across all key metrics: proven and probable reserves rose 74% to 1.1 million ounces, projected annual gold output increased approximately 17% to 82,000 ounces over an eight-year mine life, after-tax net present value (NPV5%) came in at $600.6 million, and total after-tax free cash flow reached US$769.5 million. The all-in sustaining cost of $2,331 per ounce reflects Nevada heap-leach economics — elevated relative to underground high-grade, but generating strong margins at $4,000+ gold, with an implied net margin of approximately $1,670 per ounce. Active mining is extended through 2033. The feasibility confirmation at a producing mine removes development-stage risk for investors and puts Florida Canyon's reserve base and cash flow profile on a firmer footing for any future corporate transactions. With $600M+ NPV and an 8-year life now formalized, Integra enters the second half of 2026 as a more clearly monetizable asset.

headline: BANYAN NITRA: FIRST DRILL HITS 17.8 g/t AU AT ROARING FORK — New Yukon Target 25km From 8.6Moz AurMac Deposit (TSXV: BYN)
snippet: Banyan Gold Corp. (TSXV: BYN) announced July 28, 2026 that the first exploration diamond drill holes at its 100%-owned Nitra gold project in Yukon — approximately 25 km west of the 8.6 million ounce AurMac deposit — intersected visible gold and high-grade mineralization in the newly identified Roaring Fork zone: hole NT-26-001 returned 1.62 g/t gold over 5.0 metres from 75 metres depth, including 17.80 g/t gold over 0.4 metres. Bismuth-sulphosalt associations suggest a Reduced Intrusion-Related Gold System (RIRGS) similar to what occurs at AurMac itself. A separate hole at the Seattle Creek zone also logged visible gold and mineralized quartz veins. The 7,500-metre, 11-target greenfields program is designed to test whether the RIRGS gold system that hosts AurMac extends further across the Nitra district — potentially adding resource growth optionality to a company that already controls a district-scale Yukon gold position. Assays for the lower 215 metres of NT-26-001 and all of NT-26-002 and NT-26-006 remain pending.

headline: ELDORADO SKOURIES ON TRACK FOR Q3 FIRST CONCENTRATE — McIlvenna Bay Copper-Zinc Ramping to Commercial; Solid Q2 (TSX: ELD)
snippet: Eldorado Gold Corp. (TSX/NYSE: ELD/EGO) reported Q2 2026 results on July 30 confirming two major catalysts converging in Q3 2026: the Skouries copper-gold mine in northern Greece remains on track for first concentrate production in Q3, with mill expansion completion targeted by year-end 2026 and ramp-up to commercial rates in Q1 2027; and McIlvenna Bay (Saskatchewan, acquired via the Foran Mining takeover in April 2026) achieved first copper concentrate on June 7, 2026 with first zinc concentrate in July 2026, with commercial production ramp-up expected in Q3. Skouries will be a transformational asset for Eldorado — a long-life copper-gold porphyry in an EU jurisdiction with approximately 2,948 personnel on site as of June 30. The addition of McIlvenna Bay's 41 million pounds per year copper equivalent profile further diversifies Eldorado into critical copper supply at exactly the moment when copper market tightness is accelerating. For investors tracking multi-catalyst stories in mid-tier mining, Eldorado enters H2 2026 with potentially two asset-level step-changes materializing simultaneously.

headline: MOROCCO STRATEGIC MINERALS HITS 14.88% COPPER, 696 g/t SILVER — High Atlas Grab Samples Flag District-Scale VMS Target (TSXV: MCC)
snippet: Morocco Strategic Minerals Corp. (TSXV: MCC) announced July 29, 2026 that first-phase surface sampling at the Ouneine property in Morocco's Western High Atlas mountains returned grades of up to 14.88% copper and 696 g/t silver from 49 grab samples — with 37 of the 49 samples returning at least 1.0% copper and eight exceeding 5.29%. A separate campaign at the adjacent Aït Zekri property returned up to 4.16 g/t gold in 23 grab samples with gold confirmed at surface and in historical mining galleries. These are surface grab samples, which are inherently selective and non-representative of a mineralized body, but the grades are consistent with a volcanogenic massive sulphide (VMS) system and the company has entered an option to acquire up to 80% of a district-scale portfolio in the region. Morocco's Western High Atlas is an underexplored copper-silver district with established historical production; the first-ever systematic modern sampling here is the precursor to a planned maiden drill campaign. For investors willing to track early-stage non-Canadian exploration, the copper-silver grades at Ouneine are among the most dramatic surface results reported from an emerging play this quarter.
